name: Meraioth
overview: Meraioth was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Ahitub according to Nehemiah 11:11. His role or further details about his life are not extensively recorded in Scripture beyond this genealogical note. As a Levite, he would have been part of the priestly or temple service lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Meraioth means 'rebellious' in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God but reflects a meaningful characteristic or family heritage as recorded in Nehemiah 11:11.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Meraioth as the son of Ahitub. It is also inferred that Zadok was his father and Helkai his son, connecting him within a priestly lineage as noted in Nehemiah 11:11 and 12:15. These relationships place him within a respected Levitical family line.
scriptureSignificance: Meraioth's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the Levitical priesthood, linking him to notable priestly figures such as Zadok. His mention in Nehemiah underscores the continuity of the Levitical heritage during the post-exilic restoration period. Though not highlighted for specific deeds, his inclusion affirms the faithfulness of God's covenant people through their priestly descendants.
